item.title: Raduva says youth activists often face criticism because people feel threatened by their message and influence
item.description: Young women are being encouraged to step into leadership and have their voices heard despite the stigma, criticism and discrimination they continue to face. item.content:encoded:
Young women are being encouraged to step into leadership and have their voices heard despite the stigma, criticism and discrimination they continue to face.

Speaking during the Leaders Lounge organised by Leadership Fiji part of their 25th anniversary, Climate and Environment Activist, Founder of Young EcoChamps Fiji and the Stop Releasing Balloons campaign Anne-Mary Raduva says young women are needed in leadership spaces, including Parliament, workplaces and homes, and must be supported through strong networks and sisterhood.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Raduva shares she had mentally, emotionally and spiritually prepared herself for criticism when she entered the public sphere, adding that throughout history, youth activists have often faced criticism because people can feel threatened by their message and influence.

Raduva says her environmental advocacy began when she was 13 as she started raising awareness about balloon releases and called on the Government to classify balloon releasing as littering under Fiji's Litter Act 2008.

She says she wrote to the then Prime Minister in 2018 asking for the issue to be reconsidered, but her request was not acknowledged.

Raduva says the experience nevertheless empowered her to take further action adding she realised that simply talking about balloon releases was not enough and that she needed to find an environmentally friendly alternative to amplify the message.

Raduva encourages people to become activists within their homes, communities and workplaces and said networks could be used to challenge inequalities, question existing processes and contribute to change.

She also spoke about the financial realities behind her environmental campaigns stressing her campaigns were often planned around her mother's payday, with her mother making sure there was money for transportation, reusable and biodegradable garbage bags, gloves and light refreshments.

She recalls the challenges she faced when, at the age of 13, she was told to concentrate on her studies, get a good job and leave campaign work to adults, professionals, experts and Government leaders.

Raduva says she witnessed what she considered disrespect from some adults and professionals when young people spoke about climate change, environmental issues and sustainable development.

She also recalls being mocked by some adults, including being called balloon girl and condom girl.

During the question and answer session, Raduva said her two younger sisters were among the biggest motivations behind her climate advocacy.

She says one of her sisters is 19 while the other is eight, and she wants them to grow up in an environment where they are safe, secure and have access to resources.

Raduva also says some leaders and politicians can feel threatened when young people demand accountability and transparency.

She says her faith, her mother and her two younger sisters have been important sources of support throughout her activism journey.

Meanwhile, Anne-Mary's proud mother, Moira Vilsoni, says support for young activists must begin at home, recalling that the family stood by Anne-Mary from the age of 13 when she began her climate advocacy.

Vilsoni says the family also worked to ensure Anne-Mary's message remained authentic and that she was not used by others to promote their own climate agendas.

She says supporting her daughter also meant helping financially, particularly as Anne-Mary became more involved in activism.

As Anne-Mary moves from activism into politics, Vilsoni is urging families to support young leaders, particularly young women, and says they need a small and trusted network where they can have open and honest conversations.

item.title: Raised with Love, now giving love: Youth pastor Nancy Cakacaka shares her story on fijivillage HerStory at 7pm tomorrow
item.description: Nancy Cakacaka is a senior pastor’s wife, a youth pastor, a mentor and a woman dedicated to shaping the next generation. Lovingly known as Aunty Nancy by many young people in her community, she has devoted much of her life to guiding youths, strengthening their Christian faith and encouraging them to make positive choices.
item.content:encoded:
Nancy Cakacaka is a senior pastor’s wife, a youth pastor, a mentor and a woman dedicated to shaping the next generation.

Lovingly known as Aunty Nancy by many young people in her community, she has devoted much of her life to guiding youths, strengthening their Christian faith and encouraging them to make positive choices.

On this week’s fijivillage HerStory with Temalesi Vono, Nancy opens up about her own journey, from growing up in Bua with her grandparents after her parents separated, to the values of love, faith and discipline that shaped her upbringing.

She also shares her experiences working with young people, the challenges families and youths face today, and her message to young people to listen to their parents, stay grounded in their faith and know that they are loved.

Join us at 7pm tomorrow for fijivillage HerStory with Temalesi Vono, as we hear Aunty Nancy's story.

item.title: SPCA Fiji to lodge Police complaint over viral video of dog being thrown by a teenager
item.description: SPCA Fiji will lodge a formal complaint with Police after a disturbing video went viral showing a teenager grabbing one of the dogs and throwing it into the air. SPCA Fiji has strongly condemned the incident, describing the behaviour as disgusting and unacceptable.
item.content:encoded:
SPCA Fiji will lodge a formal complaint with Police after a disturbing video went viral showing a teenager grabbing one of the dogs and throwing it into the air.

SPCA Fiji has strongly condemned the incident, describing the behaviour as disgusting and unacceptable.

It says the dogs were not harming or threatening anyone and were subjected to cruel and unnecessary treatment.

SPCA Fiji says incidents like this could also be one of the reasons stray or roaming dogs become fearful or aggressive towards people.

It says when animals are deliberately teased, chased, frightened or harmed, they can experience severe stress and fear, which may lead to defensive behaviour.

SPCA Fiji is urging people not to harm, tease, chase or provoke animals for social media likes, views, laughs or entertainment, saying such behaviour is cruel and irresponsible and can put both animals and people at risk.

It says it will not tolerate the mistreatment of animals and will continue pursuing the matter until justice is served.

SPCA Fiji has also warned that people who deliberately harm or mistreat animals for online content could face legal action.

It says animals are not props for social media content or entertainment and deserve to be treated with compassion, care and respect.

SPCA Fiji is also calling on members of the public to report any cases of animal cruelty they witness.

item.title: Funeral of Sigatoka man who died following an alleged assault to be held tomorrow
item.description: The funeral of 38-year-old Vimal Nand who died following an alleged assault will he held in Kulukulu, Sigatoka tomorrow. Police say no charges have been laid against the father and son who remain in custody as investigations continue.
item.content:encoded:
The funeral of 38-year-old Vimal Nand who died following an alleged assault will he held in Kulukulu, Sigatoka tomorrow.

Police say no charges have been laid against the father and son who remain in custody as investigations continue.

It is alleged that Nand and his sons were assaulted by the two suspects following a confrontation over an incident involving one of Nand’s farm animals.

Meanwhile, a Sigatoka resident has alleged that the suspects were drunk at the time and had brutally assaulted Nand and his two sons.

item.title: Mother demands answers after 16-year-old daughter allegedly slapped by teacher
item.description: A frustrated mother has raised concerns after her 16-year-old daughter was allegedly slapped by a teacher at Gospel High School last Thursday. The mother Neeshu Chand says the incident happened at around 3.30pm on 6th August when her husband went to pick up their daughter from school.
item.content:encoded:
A frustrated mother has raised concerns after her 16-year-old daughter was allegedly slapped by a teacher at Gospel High School last Thursday.

The mother Neeshu Chand says the incident happened at around 3.30pm on 6th August when her husband went to pick up their daughter from school.

She says her daughter told him that a teacher had slapped her on the right side of her face.

According to Chand, her daughter was waiting at her usual pick-up area when a teacher allegedly instructed students to go to a different classroom.

Speaking to fijivillage News, she says when her daughter questioned why she had to go to the classroom as she was waiting for her father, the teacher allegedly slapped her and told her she had an attitude problem.

Chand alleges her daughter then asked the teacher for her name, but the teacher refused to identify herself and allegedly grabbed the student by her school uniform and pushed her towards the classroom.

She says her daughter later asked another teacher for the identity of the teacher involved but was not given her name.

Insert: Chand on her daughter's assault 11th Aug

The mother says her daughter was then prevented from leaving the classroom to report the matter to the school office.

She says her husband and daughter later confronted the teacher with the assistance of the student's class teacher.

Chand says the teacher initially denied slapping her daughter and said she did not remember doing so.

She says the teacher later stated that if she had slapped her daughter, there would have been marks on her face, before eventually admitting that she had slapped the student and saying she was stressed and overloaded.

Chand also says the teacher later explained that students had been instructed to wait in a particular classroom because of a new rule introduced about two weeks earlier.

She says parents had not been informed about the rule and that the teacher told them it had been introduced following reported incidents of molestation in the school's waiting area.

Chand says both her daughter and a student who witnessed the alleged incident provided written statements to the school.

According to the mother, the matter was also reported to Samabula Police Station and her daughter received medical attention.

She says Police told the family that officers would follow up with the student's father and interview the teacher.

The mother says she later contacted the Police Station after receiving no update and was told that the officer handling the case was on a day off.

She says she was told another officer would be assigned to progress the matter and provide feedback by midday, but she had not received any feedback.

Chand says she also emailed the Ministry of Education on the evening of 6th August but did not receive an acknowledgement.

She says she later contacted the Ministry and was told officials were aware of the incident after receiving information from the school.

The mother says she had also forwarded her complaint to Ministry of Education officials and the Fiji Human Rights and Anti-Discrimination Commission but had not received a response.

She says her daughter returned to school on Tuesday because she was concerned about missing classes ahead of her examinations.

The mother says her husband also spoke with the principal to seek assurances about their daughter's safety and what measures would be put in place while the matter is being dealt with.

Chand says the family remains concerned about the lack of communication from the school, the Ministry and Police.

The mother is calling for clarity on what immediate measures are being taken to ensure her daughter's safety at school and what action is being taken in relation to the alleged assault.

Questions have been sent to Police, the Ministry of Education, and Fiji Human Rights and Anti-Discrimination Commission.
